newsitem.title: GEORGIA: SOCCER-FOUR PLAYERS AXED FOR LACK OF PATRIOTISM.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FOUR PLAYERS AXED FOR LACK OF PATRIOTISM.

text.p: Georgia's soccer federation has decided to axe four players accused of lacking patriotism, demanding too much money and organising an in-flight "boozy party", an official said on Wednesday.

Federation vice-president Nodar Adriadze said national coach David Kipiani had been told to drop Kakhaber Tskhadadze of Russia's Alania Vladikavkaz, Gocha Dzhamarauli of Turkey's Trapzonspor, and Mikhail Kavelashvili and Georgy Nemsadze of Switzerland's Grasshopper Zurich.
He said they had been accused of a lack of patriotism and will to win after a World Cup qualifier against Poland on June 14 which Georgia lost 4-1.
"They kept demanding money which did not match their contribution and arranged a boozy party on the plane on the way back from Poland," Adriadze told Reuters.
The players were not immediately available for comment.
Georgia are out of contention for a place in the World Cup finals after collecting only three points from five qualifying matches, leaving them trailing Italy, England and Poland.
